record.original_question: For an irreducible Markov modulated Poisson process (MMPP), does the first inter-event time in the time-stationary version stochastically dominate the first inter-event time in the event-stationary version? In the paper's notation, if T_1^pi is the first inter-event time under time-stationary initialization and T_1^alpha is the first inter-event time under event-stationary initialization, must T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha hold for every irreducible MMPP?

evidence.quote: Lemma 2.1. Consider a simple non-transient point process on the line, and let T_1^pi, T_1^alpha represent the first inter-event time in the time-stationary case and event-stationary case respectively.
Conjecture 4.2. For an irreducible MMPP, T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{J(t)\}_{t\ge 0}$ be an irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on a finite state space $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with generator matrix $Q$ and unique stationary distribution $\pi$. Let $\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)$ with $\lambda_i\ge 0$ and $\sum_i \pi_i\lambda_i>0$. Conditional on the trajectory of $J$, let $N$ be an inhomogeneous Poisson process with intensity $\lambda_{J(t)}$ at time $t$. The pair $(J,N)$ is the (irreducible) Markov-modulated Poisson process (MMPP).

Two natural stationary initializations of the MMPP on $\mathbb{R}$ are:
- The time-stationary version: the law under which the joint process $(J(t),N)$ is invariant under time shifts; equivalently, $J(0)$ is distributed according to $\pi$. Let $T_1^\pi$ denote the time from $0$ to the first event of $N$ after $0$ under this law.
- The event-stationary (Palm) version: the law obtained by Palm-conditioning on an event of $N$ at time $0$; equivalently, $J(0)$ is distributed according to $\alpha$, where $\alpha_i = \pi_i\lambda_i / \sum_j \pi_j\lambda_j$. Let $T_1^\alpha$ denote the time from $0$ to the next event of $N$ after $0$ under this law.

Prove or disprove: for every irreducible MMPP,
$$T_1^\pi \ge_{\mathrm{st}} T_1^\alpha,$$
i.e. $\Pr(T_1^\pi > t) \ge \Pr(T_1^\alpha > t)$ for all $t\ge 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The stochastic dominance statement is posed as a conjecture for general irreducible MMPPs. It has been verified in special cases, in particular for Markov-switched Poisson processes (MSPPs) and for order-two MMPPs, but a proof (or counterexample) for general irreducible MMPPs does not appear in the available literature, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Stationary Markovian Arrival Processes: Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses stationary MAPs/MMPPs with conjectures regarding stochastic ordering of time-stationary versus event-stationary inter-event times, proven for special cases including order-two MMPPs and MSPPs.
status_evidence.claim: The stochastic dominance T_1^pi >=st T_1^alpha is stated as an open conjecture for general irreducible MMPPs, with proofs only in special cases.
